items.title: 2,800-year-old bone flute found at Troy, first instrument in 160 years of digs
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: For the first time in 160 years, archaeologists unearthed a bone flute at Troy, dating back approximately 2,800 years. In addition, they found a humanoid idol from the Early Bronze Age, offering new insights into the region's cultural traditions. The discoveries were announced by Turkish Minister of Culture and Tourism, Mehmet Nuri Ersoy. This time period correlates with the legendary works of Greek poet Homer.
